assumptions: The scaffold stubs described in docs/decisions/0002 are on the base branch as each unit says, including the MainDeps members `openDatabase` and `configureServer` and the stub files under src/db, src/tenancy and src/api.
`web/dist` is built by the build gate before the test and e2e gates run (add-web-shell F-1), and react-router 7.18.4 is already installed and exact-pinned (F-2).
The root `pnpm run test` script runs src/**, test/** and web/src/** test files under --test-global-setup, as the units claim between them.
The ordering in src/main.ts is the same across units: openDatabase before buildServer (db-foundation), then registerWebApp (web-shell), then configureServer (e2e-stack), then listen.

No source code delivered by add-db-foundation or add-tenancy-foundation breaks the add-architecture-fitness rules (no console, process.env, network imports or deep imports), whatever order those units merge in.

findings.text: The fatal startup line's `msg` rule is contradicted between add-engine-skeleton and add-e2e-stack, which depends on it. add-engine-skeleton decision 9 says `msg` is `startup failed: <ConfigError message>` for a ConfigError, "else `startup failed`", and that "Later units reuse this line for their codes". Decision 12 limits the error text on the fatal line to the ConfigError message (no value). Its scenario "Startup failures refuse start" asserts that `new Error("boom")` gives `msg` "startup failed" and no `boom`. add-e2e-stack decision 2 says a `configureServer` throw writes `{ code, msg }` with "`msg` its `message`", and its scenario "A throwing hook stops the start" asserts `msg` "hook failed", which is the raw error message of a plain Error. So a dependent unit sets aside a stated no-error-text rule of its dependency, and a test enforces the change. The author has to pick one: either e2e-stack uses `startup failed` on the hook path, or engine-skeleton decision 9 states the exception and why it is safe.

add-web-shell sits between the two conflicting fatal-line rules and does not say what `msg` carries for a `WebAppError`. Its Interfaces (src/main.ts note) say "the single fatal line { code, msg } of add-engine-skeleton", which gives `startup failed`. Its decision 15 says the WebAppError line is written "as add-e2e-stack does for configureServer", which gives the error's message. The scenario "A bad directory stops the start" checks only `code` "WEB_DIST_INVALID" and that no path appears, so both readings pass. The two units' implementations can therefore diverge without any test failing.

add-e2e-stack decision 12 says engine sessions are found "by excluding the two known pool names, since the pool's default name is not pinned". add-db-foundation pins that default: "`PoolOptions` defaults 10, 5000, 30000, unset, `\"ursitoare\"`" (applicationName). The scenario "Health reports the database" still works by exclusion, so this is only stale wording. It could instead assert `application_name` = `ursitoare` for the engine's sessions.

add-db-foundation's scenario "No database keeps /health green" calls `startServer(0)` with no host. add-engine-skeleton gives the signature `startServer(port: number, host?: string)` but never states the default host. Its own scenario always passes "127.0.0.1", and decision 11's `url` rule depends on the host. The db-foundation scenario checks only `typeof running.url`, so nothing breaks, but the shared interface leaves the default undecided.

missing: The root package.json `test` script and its globs. add-architecture-fitness says it runs `test/**/*.test.ts`, add-web-shell says it already covers `web/src/**/*.test.ts`, and add-engine-skeleton relies on `src/**/*.test.ts`.

The .gitignore contents. add-architecture-fitness's secret scan reads every untracked file that is not ignored, and the build gate creates `web/dist` (and any tsc output) before `pnpm run test`. Whether those directories are ignored was not shown.

The scaffold stub contents (docs/decisions/0002). I could not check that the base-branch stubs under src/db, src/tenancy and src/api already meet the architecture rules that add-architecture-fitness's repo test applies to them.

assumptions: `git` is on PATH in the gate and the gate runs inside a git work tree, as proposal 'Interfaces taken' and design decision 10 state.
The Node test runner runs the `test/arch/*.ts` files directly with type stripping, and `typescript` 6.0.3 is importable as `import ts from "typescript"`, as the design Context states.

`add-engine-skeleton` is merged before this unit runs. The facts listed under 'Facts that add-engine-skeleton delivers' hold as the orchestrator asserts; any that does not hold ends the unit through the defined blocker path, not through wrong code.

The module graph table was checked by hand: 30 keys in the listed order, 26 names for `api` and `cli`, `publish` with 12 names, the version 3 edges, and no cycle. The expected orders in the multi-file scenarios ("A require call is a value import", "createRequire is refused", "The snapshot reads a real directory") were checked against the sort rule of decision 11.
`pnpm run test` collects the `test/arch/*.test.ts` files this unit adds. The design Context gives the glob `test/**/*.test.ts`.

findings.text: In design.md, the Test plan says "`git` runs only on temp repositories built with `git init` and `git add`". But the scenario "The merged tree is clean" (architecture-rules) and task 5.1 run `scanRepository` over the repository root, and that runs `git ls-files` in the real repository. The real-tree scan is clearly the intended behaviour, so the Test plan sentence should be corrected.

Decision 10 lists files with `git ls-files -co --exclude-standard` and does not say to use `-z`. With git's default `core.quotePath`, a path containing non-ASCII bytes is printed C-quoted. That quoted name does not exist on disk, so the rule 'listed files that no longer exist are skipped' silently drops a real file from the secret scan. The Failure cases table also leaves a gap: a deleted file is 'skipped without error' and 'an unreadable file propagates the read error', but a file that exists at listing time and is gone (ENOENT) at read time fits neither. The spec should require NUL-separated output (or decoding of quoted paths) and say how ENOENT on read is treated.

Decision 5 lists the module-graph conditions independently: not in `MODULES` gives `ARCH_UNKNOWN_MODULE`, not in `allowed` gives `ARCH_MODULE_EDGE`, and a target other than `index.ts` gives `ARCH_DEEP_IMPORT`. It does not say whether one import that meets several of them reports one violation or several. Examples are an import that is both a disallowed edge and a deep path, or an import of an unknown module, which is never in `allowed` either. The scenarios say a file "gets" a code and never "only" that code (e.g. "Unknown directories are refused"). Later rules and the exact-output assertions in the test plan depend on the answer, so state precedence or exclusivity.

Decision 5 reports an unknown `src/<dir>` at `src/<dir>:1`. It does not say how the files inside that directory are judged, because `MODULES[M]` is undefined there. Are their cross-module imports checked, skipped or reported, and is the module treated as having no egress in the network rule (decision 7)? An implementer can infer an answer, but the spec should state it.

Two outputs are left to the implementer:
- In "A new egress capability is refused", the third case ("an `egress` value outside `tools`, `oidc`, `otlp` is reported too") has no fixture value and no expected text.
- The return form of `listScannableFiles` is not given: repository-relative or absolute paths, and in what order. Yet "The file list covers tracked and untracked files only" asserts it returns "exactly" three files.
Both should be fixed so the test is decided by the spec, not by the implementer.

The two requirements of capability `architecture-tree-blockers` ("A violation in a file this change may not change is a blocker" and "The merged tree meets the facts this change relies on") describe what the implementer should do and list facts about the orchestrator's environment. No test can decide them. Because they are written as a capability, they would be archived as a permanent spec of the product.

Requirement "No console in src" says `checkConsole` SHALL fail "any use of `console`". Design decision 9 limits the rule to a property or element access on `console` or `globalThis.console`, plus value imports from `node:console` or `console`. Under decision 9, a bare reference such as `const c = console; c.log(x)` passes. The requirement text should match the narrower rule, or the rule should be widened.

Decision 1 scans only `.ts .mts .cts .tsx .js .mjs .cjs` files. The test-file pattern `/\.test\.[cm]?[jt]sx?$/` does match `.jsx`, so a non-test `src/**/*.jsx` file escapes every rule. This is a nit, since Node does not load `.jsx` without a loader, but the two lists should agree.

assumptions: The scaffold stubs and installed packages (`pg`, `@types/pg`, `embedded-postgres`, the `@embedded-postgres/*` binaries) are on the base branch, as both proposals say.
`add-engine-skeleton` is merged as specified before this unit starts, including the optional `MainDeps.openDatabase` and `configureServer` members.
The test run is not executed as root, since Postgres refuses to start as root and no option for that is mentioned.

The Node version in use supports `--test-global-setup` and passes the `process.env.TEST_PG_CLUSTER` set in `globalSetup` on to the test-file child processes, which the base `pnpm run test` script and the design rely on.

findings.text: The design says `createPool` parses the URL with `new URL` (Decision 2, task 1.1), and the pool scenario expects `"not a url"` → `bad_scheme` but `"postgres://u@/d"` → `missing_host`. Under WHATWG URL parsing, userinfo followed by an empty host is a parse failure, so `new URL("postgres://u@/d")` throws the same TypeError as `new URL("not a url")`. The spec gives no rule for turning a `new URL` failure into a `details.reason`, so the implementer has to invent a pre-check that the scenario pins only for these seven inputs. Any other unparseable postgres URL, such as one with an out-of-range port, has no specified reason. The fix is to state the rule: for example, check the scheme on the raw string first, then treat any parse failure of a postgres or postgresql URL as a stated reason.

The fatal startup line for a `DbError` has no clear rule. design.md § Context says the skeleton's fatal line takes `code` and `reason` "from the error's `code` and `details.reason`" and that this unit "reuses it". But the given `ConfigError` has `code`, `variable` and a constructor `reason`, with no `details` member. The skeleton also lists `STARTUP_FAILED` for failures that are not config errors, and its proposal says the fatal `msg` carries the `ConfigError` message. So the claim cannot describe how the merged `main` treats its own errors. Task 10.1 says only "on a throw write the fatal line". It does not say whether `main.ts`'s error-to-line mapping changes, or which errors have their `code`/`details.reason` copied. If the implementer copies any string `error.code`, the skeleton's listen-failure line (for example `EADDRINUSE`) would get a new label. The skeleton's expected codes for `new Error("boom")` and the port-in-use case are in the cut part of engine-runtime/spec.md, so the material cannot show that the merged tests would catch this. The fix is to state the `DbError` branch explicitly: which errors are recognised, which fields they give, and that `msg` is `"startup failed"`.

Some defaults and failure codes are missing. `createDbHealthCheck(pool, opts?: { timeoutMs?: number })` has no default or bounds for `timeoutMs`, and nothing says what value `openDatabase` passes when it registers `db`. Out-of-range `lockTimeoutMs` (1-600000) and `openTimeoutMs` (0-600000) have no error code or reason; `bad_option` is only stated for `PoolOptions` and the partition window.

`migrate` sets `SET lock_timeout` at session level on its client. Nothing says whether it is reset, so it stays in force for the statements of every migration file and for the client returned to the pool. The design maps SQLSTATE 55P03 to `MIGRATION_LOCK_TIMEOUT` only in the "before any file runs" sentence. A 55P03 raised inside a file (MIGRATION_FAILED or MIGRATION_LOCK_TIMEOUT?) is unspecified. So is a connection lost in the middle of a file, where `ROLLBACK` and the `pg_advisory_unlock` in `finally` also fail, along with which error is reported then.

The `openDatabase` retry wording and its scenario do not quite match. The design says it retries "until `deps.clock` passes the deadline" and waits `min(500, remaining)`. The Postgres-down scenario expects the `sleep` calls to be exactly `[50]` with `openTimeoutMs` 50 and a clock that only `sleep` moves. On a strict "passes" (>) reading, the attempt at clock == deadline fails, then `sleep(0)` runs, and the clock never moves again, so the loop never ends. The prose should say that the loop stops when `now >= deadline`.

Some stated error outcomes have no scenario. Nothing tests `MIGRATION_ROLE_INVALID` with reason `owner_role_privileged` (owner with `rolsuper` or `rolbypassrls`). Nothing tests `ensureRoles` against a Postgres that is down, which the Failure cases section says gives `DB_UNAVAILABLE`.

The tasks do not cover the test-database requirements cleanly. "App pool obeys RLS" is a scenario of the requirement "A fresh database per test", but only task 6.1 (`base.test.ts`, which claims "Base migration and grants model") runs it. Task 2.1 claims "A fresh database per test", and its coverage list leaves this scenario out.

`openDatabase` logs a warn from the app pool's `onError`, but the log object and message are not given. Security §4 forbids a driver message in any log line, so the expected shape (for example `{ code, reason }` and a fixed `msg`) should be stated.

The spec claims more about owner credentials than the code enforces. The proposal and Security §4 say the engine "never holds the owner credentials". Yet the engine's `loadConfig` reads `URSITOARE_DATABASE_OWNER_PASSWORD_FILE` when set, and the "Database configured" engine-boot scenario passes `ownerEndpoint` with its password to `main`. In the material, keeping the owner password out of the engine depends only on the deployment (D-3). The code only guarantees that the engine never opens `database.owner`.

The order of `server.close()` and `database.close()` inside main's shutdown `close` is not stated. If the database closes first, requests still draining see `db: fail`. Also, when the URL has no port, the value `createPool` passes to `pg.Pool` is not stated.

assumptions: The four prerequisite units are merged into the target before this unit starts, as the plan states, and their delivered behaviour matches the specs shown.

The browser e2e gate runs `node test/support/e2e-stack/main.ts` with `E2E_PROFILE` unset (so `fake`), one test at a time against a single stack, so `injected_fault` and `fresh_state` do not interfere across tests.
In `test_fresh_state_clears_faults`, `injected_fault` is set up before `fresh_state` is requested (for example via `request.getfixturevalue`), as the scenario's wording implies.
`e2e/test_health.py::test_health_reports_ok` asserts `status` ok and not an exact `checks` body, so it keeps passing once `checks.db` appears.
`createPool` from add-db-foundation installs a pool error handler, so `DROP DATABASE ... WITH (FORCE)` during a reset does not crash the engine or the test pools.

The cross-unit shapes I checked line up: `sequentialIds(1)` gives tenant id `ten_...0001`, `URSITOARE_DATABASE_URL` without sslmode or password passes engine-config, and the engine key file of 64 hex characters meets the engine's key rule.

findings.text: Scenario "Offline start, health, SIGTERM" (and the stack.db.test.ts plan in task 5.2 and the design.md Test plan) says `dns.lookup` and `dns.promises.lookup` are mocked in-process while a stack starts, resets and closes, and that they record zero calls. Node's `net.Server.prototype.listen` with a `host` option goes through `lookupAndListen`, which calls `dns.lookup(host, ...)` every time, including for an IP literal. The IP shortcut is inside `dns.lookup`, not before the call. The stack opens two listeners that way: the engine's Fastify `listen` on `127.0.0.1` (URSITOARE_HOST=127.0.0.1, decision 4) and the control listener (decision 9, `node:http` bound to `127.0.0.1`). The `dns` module that `net` loads internally is the same exports object a test mocks through `node:dns`, so the mock will record at least two calls per start. As written, the assertion cannot pass. An implementer that cannot ask will either be stuck on a red test or quietly narrow it (for example to 'no lookup of a non-IP hostname'), and that rewritten assertion would merge unread. The author should say what counts as name resolution: lookups of non-IP hostnames only, or resolver/`dns.promises` calls only.

Decision 1 calls `main({ loadConfig, destination, signals, exit, configureServer })` without `openDatabase`, but the stack scenarios expect `checks.db` "ok". That works only if `main` falls back to the real `src/db` `openDatabase` when none is injected. add-db-foundation's requirement text suggests this, but every scenario shown injects a spy, and its design is truncated in the material. design.md § Context restates every other dependency shape and does not restate this default. Restate it, or pass `openDatabase` explicitly.

Scenario "Bad options, busy port" (`details.fatal` containing `EADDRINUSE`) and the process scenario "Bad variable or busy port" depend on the engine writing `EADDRINUSE` into its fatal line when listen fails. design.md § Context does not restate the engine's fatal-line content for that case. The fatal shape it does show is `{ code, msg, variable?, reason?, host?, port? }`, and add-db-foundation uses `msg` "startup failed". So it is not established that the error's code reaches the line.

Decision 4 lists `URSITOARE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` among the stack's env keys but gives no value, while every other key has one or is derived (`_ROLE=all`, `_HOST=127.0.0.1`, `_LOG_LEVEL=info`, `_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_MS=2000`). Parts can see it through `PartContext.env`, so its value should be stated, presumably `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`.

`checkControlRoutes` fixes the code `ARCH_CONTROL_ROUTE`, file and line, but not the message text. add-architecture-fitness requires 'Every message says how to fix the violation', and its other rules pin exact messages.

The process failure table says a SIGTERM/SIGINT during the start leads to 'the start settles, the stack closes, no ready line, exit 0', and the process requirement says any start error prints `e2e stack failed: ...` and exits 1. The case where a signal arrives during the start and the start then rejects is covered by both, with different exit codes and stderr output. Pick one.

Control listener (decision 9, task 3.3): only an `E2eStackError` rejection from `reset()` (500 `STACK_RESET_FAILED` with `details.part`) and `FaultInvalidError` (400) are mapped. The status and code are not stated for a `reset()` rejection of another type, or for an unexpected throw while handling `POST /faults`. The envelope's `message` for `STACK_RESET_FAILED` is also not stated.

Scenario "Health reports the database" requires every `pg_stat_activity` row for `ursitoare_e2e` whose `application_name` is neither `e2e-stack` nor `e2e-test` to use `ursitoare_app`. An autovacuum worker on that database has neither name and is not `ursitoare_app`, so the assertion can fail intermittently. Also filter on `backend_type = 'client backend'`.

missing: The truncated THEN clause of add-engine-skeleton's "Startup failures refuse start" scenario: whether the fatal line for a listen failure carries `EADDRINUSE`. If it does not, the `details.fatal` assertions in this unit cannot pass, and that would raise the interfaces finding to major.

add-db-foundation design.md (truncated): whether `main` defaults `MainDeps.openDatabase` to the real implementation, and whether `startCluster` puts the cluster directory under `os.tmpdir()`. The TMPDIR/`PG_VERSION` and `postmaster.pid` assertions of this unit depend on the second.

Whether `embedded-postgres` installs its own process signal or exit hooks at module load (for example through `async-exit-hook`) that stop clusters and call `process.exit` with a non-zero code. If so, they would race the stack process's SIGTERM handler and the scenarios requiring exit code 0. This would be a second major failure_cases finding if confirmed.
add-e2e-stack has no hidden files; its tasks.md, design.md, proposal.md and spec were all shown. The prerequisites' tasks.md and some design.md files were not shown.

assumptions: The scaffold (docs/decisions/0002) is already on the base branch, with signature stubs for every listed interface and fastify 5.12.7 and pino 10.4.0 installed, so depends_on: [] is correct.
On Fastify 5.12.7, a malformed JSON body produces a 400 error with an FST_ERR_CTP* code (e.g. FST_ERR_CTP_INVALID_JSON_BODY), as decision 4's mapping order requires.
On Fastify 5.12.7, `request.routeOptions.url` is undefined in the not-found context, so the `"unmatched"` fallback applies to /nope.
With `return503OnClosing: false`, Fastify 5.12.7 routes a pipelined request on a kept-alive socket during close and sets `Connection: close`, as the drain scenario expects.
Pino 10.4.0's redaction accepts the listed paths: `*.` prefixes from 0 to 3 levels deep, and bracket notation for `set-cookie`.
Pino 10.4.0 copies `err.message` into `msg` when no message is given, as decision 8 says was checked.
`ConfigError.message` is `<variable>: <reason>`, as implied by the table header and the main startup-failure scenario.
When a custom error handler and not-found handler are set, Fastify does not log errors itself, so `hunter2` appears only where the spec's own log calls put it.

findings.text: Scenario "Bad values are refused without echoing them" requires "no offending value in the message", but one listed input can't be decided by a substring check. For URSITOARE_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_MS="0", the fixed reason text "must be an integer from 1 to 300000" contains the character "0", so `!message.includes(value)` fails even when the code is correct. The other inputs are clean: port "0" vs "65535", "1e3", " 5", "+5", "300001", "verbose", "boss", "bad host", "http://h", "ftp://x" and the credential URL. Fix: state the expected message as exact equality with `<variable>: <reason text>` from the configuration table, at least for that input.

proposal.md says "Every error response is { error: { code, message, details? } } with an x-request-id header", and Security §5 lists "token in a URL" as an abuse case. Design decision 3 fixes the complete Fastify option set and leaves out `frameworkErrors`. Fastify answers framework-level errors such as a malformed percent-encoded path (FST_ERR_BAD_URL) outside the root error handler and outside `onSend`. That response has Fastify's own body, which echoes the path, and no x-request-id. No scenario says what happens there. Either state the behaviour (for example, set `frameworkErrors` to route through `toErrorResponse` and add a bad-URL scenario) or narrow the outcome claim.

`installGracefulShutdown(opts)` declares `signals?: SignalSource` but never says what it defaults to: `process`, or no signal listeners at all. `main` gets defaults for its own deps ("signals to process"), but this exported function, which later units can call, doesn't.

Two things about `main` are unspecified. First, which `forceClose` it passes to `installGracefulShutdown`, if any (for example, `server.server.closeAllConnections`); 'force-close the remaining connections' depends on it. Second, what `RunningServer.close()` returned by `main` does about the installed signal handlers (call `dispose()` or leave them).

`startServer(port, host?)` makes `host` optional, but the material never says the default host or the resulting `RunningServer.url` when `host` is omitted. Decision 11 only covers a configured host. The answer presumably sits in the base-branch `src/main.ts`, which isn't shown.

The `Secret` class signature in § Interfaces lists `reveal`, `toJSON` and `toString` only. The design notes and the "No secret byte leaves the config object" scenario also require `[util.inspect.custom]` to return "[REDACTED]". The exported shape is incomplete.

`URSITOARE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` says "trailing / removed" but not whether the result is the raw string minus one slash or a URL-normalized form (lower-cased host, default port dropped). The scenario only uses an already-normalized lower-case input.
The test plan says "no network beyond loopback port 0", but "main starts and stops" also requires a run with host "0.0.0.0", which binds all interfaces.

Decision 9 defines the fatal line's `reason` field (a string `details.reason`, e.g. DB_ROLE_UNSAFE gives `superuser`), but no scenario in this unit exercises it. Separately, "a bad query or path parameter reports querystring/n or params/id" names no concrete route schema or input value, so the test has to invent them.

"Tracer port" says the span ends "when the response is sent, whatever the tracer does", and the scenario asserts "each ended once". Neither says what happens to a span when the client aborts before the response finishes (`onResponse` may not run), or whether `end()` still runs when `setAttribute` throws inside the shared try/catch.

The `err` serializer (task 2.1) is specified only for Error instances that have a `stack`. It doesn't say what to log for a thrown non-Error value (a string or plain object), or for an Error whose `stack` is undefined or non-string.

findings.text: The gate only covers the workspace projects that exist today. `MANIFEST_PATHS` is fixed to `["package.json", "web/package.json"]` and the policy file is frozen. Design Decision 2 says pnpm runs `preinstall`…`postprepare` "of each workspace project", and the proposal's Why names "the lifecycle scripts of the workspace projects". Even so, nothing checks that `packages` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` resolves only to those two directories. A later unit that adds a workspace member with a `postinstall` script or a `^` range passes every test. This gap is not in the Security "Not detected" list. Fix: either assert that `packages` matches the `MANIFEST_PATHS` directories, or list the gap as not detected.

The `.npmrc` rule only looks at lines of the form `key=value` ("a line `key=value` of `.npmrc` … whose key (text before the first `=`…)"). In ini format, a bare line such as `dangerously-allow-all-builds` is usually read as `true` (this is outside knowledge, not in the material). Such a line would not be reported, yet Security §4 claims that every `.npmrc` setting that widens builds has a failing scenario. Fix: treat a bare key that is not a comment as a setting, or list the case as not detected.

`topLevelKeys` and `readTopLevelList` only recognise `<key>:` at column 0. Other YAML spellings of a top-level key are missed: `key :`, explicit `? key`, a flow mapping at column 0, merge keys, and quoted keys with escapes. Such a key in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` would pass silently. Fix: refuse top-level lines that are not recognised, or add these forms to "Not detected".

`scanNpmStore` keeps "every entry that is not a symlink" in `<dir>/node_modules` and has no rule for a real entry that is not a package, such as a dot-directory. It depends on the layout the design asserts ("one real package directory plus symlinks"). If any such entry exists, it shows up as `npm <name>@unknown` with `LICENCE_MISSING`, and the live npm test fails. Decision 4 allows fixing the reader, but the skip rule is not specified.

Two fallbacks are missing: a `METADATA` file that exists but has no `Name` or `Version` header, and a store `package.json` that is valid JSON but has no `name` or `version` string. The name/version fallback is only defined for a missing `METADATA` or a missing or invalid `package.json`. Failure cases says "invalid" `METADATA` gives `LICENCE_MISSING`, but never defines what "invalid" means for header text.

Some violation details are not fully defined. "Built dependency details" joins "the parts that apply" but does not say whether `missing: [...]` also applies when the key is absent or its form is unsupported. Only the third case's detail is spelled out; "A missing workspace file fails" fixes only the prefix `key not found`. The separators inside multi-item lists are also unspecified: `terms not on the allowlist: a, b`? `[a, b]` or `[a,b]`?

Design Decisions says "A live test asserts once, with `formatLicenceViolations(...)` as the message". Two live tests check more than one thing:
- `the licence policy data is well formed` checks that `checkPolicy` returns `[]`, that `LICENCE_EXCEPTIONS` holds exactly one entry, and the five fixed export values.
- "The current venv passes" requires both a pass and that a separate `exceptions: []` call returns exactly one `LICENCE_UNKNOWN`.

Decision 1 says "The owner may narrow the set by editing `test/arch/licence-policy.ts`". But "The reviewed policy values are fixed" pins `ALLOWED_LICENCES` to the exact 11 values inside `licences.test.ts`, so narrowing the set also requires a test edit. That may be intended as double entry, but the spec does not say so.

`pythonLicenceOf(metadata: string)` takes no classifier map, but it must map leaves through `PYPI_CLASSIFIER_SPDX`. So `licence-rules.ts` has to import that value from `licence-policy.ts`, or copy reviewed data into ordinary code. The spec states neither. Its claim that the types live in rules "so the stubs typecheck without it" holds only for the stubs. Fix: say that rules imports the value from policy.

Decision 4 says "admitting a licence is the owner's edit of the policy file", and decisions 1–5 are recorded as made by the orchestrator. The `text-unidecode@1.3` exception (Artistic/GPL) is recorded only under "Decisions made while writing 2", with no owner or orchestrator approval noted. The unattended implementer will write it into the policy file. Whether to admit it is a product decision this review does not make; only its missing approval record is noted.

assumptions: add-engine-skeleton and add-db-foundation are merged into main before this unit starts, with the exact interfaces restated in this unit's design.md (ROLE_OWNER/ROLE_APP values, withTestDatabase cloning a template migrated with every file in DEFAULT_MIGRATIONS_DIR, sequentialIds default seed 0).

db-foundation's role-changing tests (`ALTER ROLE ursitoare_app BYPASSRLS`, `GRANT ursitoare_owner TO ursitoare_app`, the 'Migration preconditions' scenarios) run on a separate cluster, not the shared test cluster. Scenario (a) needs `ursitoare_app` to be absent, which suggests this. Otherwise this unit's 'The migrated database is clean' catalog checks would flake, because roles are cluster-wide.
A database cloned with CREATE DATABASE … TEMPLATE keeps the default PUBLIC TEMP privilege, so the app role can create the shadowing temp table in 'A shadowing temp table changes nothing'.
Postgres 18.4 allows a superuser to create a FOREIGN DATA WRAPPER with no handler, and allows a foreign table on it to be created and granted without ever being queried.
Test pools created with createPool(db.appEndpoint, { max: 1 }) are ended before db.close() drops the database.

findings.text: design.md § Test plan says the `note` probe table has "RLS enabled and forced". db-foundation's `ensureRoles` makes sure `ursitoare_owner` is neither superuser nor `BYPASSRLS`, so with FORCE on, the owner is subject to `note_isolation` (`tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id', true)`). The owner-side checks in tx.test.ts then prove nothing or fail. In "Rollback when fn throws" and "A caught SQL error fails closed", "the owner sees no note" returns zero rows whether or not anything was committed, so the 'nothing committed' assertion can never fail. In "Tenant A cannot read or write tenant B rows", "the owner inserted one note per tenant" fails the WITH CHECK (42501) unless the owner sets `app.tenant_id` for each row, and "the owner sees tenant B's note unchanged and no `n9`" again reads nothing. Compare db-foundation's "App pool obeys RLS", which inserts rows before RLS is forced and checks them through the superuser on `adminUrl`. The spec must say how `note` rows are seeded and checked: set the tenant in the owner transaction, check through `adminUrl`, or don't force RLS on the probe table.

proposal.md says the catalog test "fails the build when a later table lacks … forced RLS or a tenant-only policy". The actual rule (design.md 'Policy rule', task 7.1) is a text match: every non-null policy expression must contain `app.tenant_id`. The spec's own scenario "A table with no key or no tenant column is reported" gives `bad_nopk` and `bad_notid` the policy `USING (current_setting('app.tenant_id', true) IS NOT NULL)` and expects no `no_tenant_policy` violation for either. So the guard accepts a policy that shows every tenant's rows to any session that has a tenant set. The outcome promised and the rule specified don't match. The author must either reword the outcome or tighten the rule; this unit is the foundation of exit test 18, and every later table depends on the guard.

Task 2.1 says to create `src/db/migrations/0002_tenancy.sql` "exactly as in design.md § Data model", and both plpgsql bodies end with an `END;` line. In Postgres, `END` is a synonym for `COMMIT`. db-foundation's `readMigrationFiles` rejects a file "holding a line `commit;`" with `MIGRATION_FAILED` / `transaction_control`, but the exact match rule is in db-foundation's design.md, which is cut from the material. The aside that "the plpgsql keyword is `BEGIN` without a semicolon" shows the author knew the detector matters, yet `END;` is not addressed. If the detector matches `end;`, the 'verbatim' instruction conflicts with the runner the unit depends on. Say whether `END;` lines are accepted, or drop the optional semicolon after the final `END` of each function body.

Task 5.1 turns "a pg error with a five-character SQLSTATE code" into `TENANT_BOOTSTRAP_FAILED`, and lets other errors propagate. design.md limits `src/tenancy` to `pg` types, so it can't do a runtime `instanceof` check against the driver's error class. Node errno codes such as `EPIPE` and `EPERM` are also five characters and would be reported as `TENANT_BOOTSTRAP_FAILED` with a bogus `details.sqlstate`. Also, no scenario covers the stated rule that a refused connection propagates from `ensureDefaultTenant`, and nothing says what `checkTenancyCatalog` does when its queries fail.

In "Tenant A cannot read or write tenant B rows", the last step inside `fn` is an insert that fails with 42501. The scenario doesn't say what `withTenantTx` itself rejects with: the 42501 error if `fn` lets it escape, or `TENANT_TX_ABORTED` if `fn` catches it to keep asserting. The test author has to pick one.

Task 7.2 says "rolsuper or rolbypassrls and membership, both `app_role_privileged <role>`", which leaves `<role>` open: the app role, or the privileged role `o` it belongs to. The scenario "The real role and probe roles" (`app_role_privileged postgres`, `app_role_privileged <probe>`) implies the app role's name. The task text should say that outright. Likewise, it should say whether `app_role_owns_relation` looks at all of `pg_class` or only schema `ursitoare`.

findings.text: ApiClient base URL rule (task 6.1): a `baseUrl` is refused only when it is "neither `""` nor starts with `/`". That rule lets through `//evil.test` and `/\evil.test`, and browsers send both to another origin. This conflicts with the requirement "ApiClient" ("SHALL send JSON requests to the same origin") and with design.md § Security item 5, which lists "another origin (\"ApiClient\")" as an abuse case that is covered. The scenario only tests `"https://x"`. Add a clause that refuses a `baseUrl` whose second character is `/` or `\`, and add a scenario input for it. This is minor because `baseUrl` is set by code, and `credentials: "same-origin"` keeps cookies from going cross-origin.

WebAppError messages: design.md § Interfaces says the `WEB_DIST_INVALID` and `WEB_APP_DUPLICATE` messages are "fixed texts without the path", but the texts are never given. The `msg` of the fatal line that `main` writes for a `WebAppError` is not stated either. It could be the error's message, or the `"startup failed"` that add-db-foundation uses for a `DbError`. The scenario "A bad directory stops the start" checks only `code` and "no path", so the implementer is not stuck. But the error interface is left open, and a later unit cannot match on it.

Feature registry rules (task 6.2) vs `routeTable` (design.md § Interfaces): `routeTable` always appends `{ id: "not-found", path: "*" }`, and `pageTitle("not-found")` returns the not-found title. The rules do not reserve the id `not-found`, which matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$`. The phrase "optionally ending in `/*`" also leaves open whether the path `/*` alone is valid. A feature registered with either one would clash silently with the catch-all route, or shadow it. Neither case appears in the "Refusals" scenario.

Task 1.1 says `src/api/security-headers.test.ts` begins with `typeof buildServer` and `typeof healthPayload`. The scenario "Success, error and not-found responses" names `typeof registerSecurityHeaders` instead. Both can be asserted, so this does no harm, but the two texts should agree.
